Go passes since A2 only because of upstream credential precedence: the env CA (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE) wins over WithInsecure in all three gRPC exporters (otlploggrpc v0.7.0 ignored it and sent logs in plaintext; v0.23.0 honours it). The helper still does not resolve https + INSECURE=true: without a CA it exports plaintext (A3, D1.c).

Asserted via the grpc-timeout header (gRPC only; HTTP timeouts stay in A3 unit tests). Python: the SDK parses *_TIMEOUT as seconds while the spec says milliseconds (design D1.e); A3 adds the helper ms→s shim. Go: the SDK applies the env since A3 (G10: the helper passes no timeout unless set in code). Bound is lte 600, not 500: grpc encodes the remaining deadline and can round it up (501m observed with timeout=0.5 s passed by the helper); 600 still separates ms (500) from a seconds misread (500000) and the 10 s default (10000).

The resource is one target_info series; each series carries the instrumentation scope as the otel_scope_name label (Go, Python and the Node serializer). Python's exporter 0.63b0 (sdk 1.42, the lower bound) writes no scope labels; 0.64b0 (sdk 1.43) does, so the case runs from sdk 1.43 (checked 2026-11-02).
Design D1 row "Disabled-metric patterns" (A21): items trimmed, blank items ignored; * matches any run of characters, dots included.
Design D1 row "Disabled-metric patterns" (A21): ? matches exactly one character (parity.payloa?? needs two after payloa, so parity.payload is kept).
Design D1 row "Disabled-metric patterns" (A21): [ is literal (no classes), so parity.[pr]* drops nothing (Go path.Match and Python fnmatch read it as a class).
Design D1 row "Disabled-metric patterns" (A21): matching is case-sensitive (the Python SDK View lower-cases its pattern).

Design D1 row "Colliding label names" (B7/A21 fix round): attribute keys that collide once sanitized (a.b, a_b) become one label, the values sorted and joined with ;, on data points and on target_info (Go's exporter; Prometheus rejects a repeated label name).

Design D1 row "Colliding label names" (final round): the merged values are sorted as strings, not ordered by key (Go exporter.go:652 and :692, slices.Sort(vals)): a.b="y", a_b="x" give a_b="x;y"; the resource twin x.y=2, x_y=1 gives x_y="1;2".

Design D1 row "Suffix semantics": the unit word is added unless the name already ends with it (probe.bytes-sent in By). Go's otlptranslator v1.0.0 works on name tokens and drops a unit word found anywhere (metric_namer.go:273-276, removeItem): probe_bytes_sent_total.

Design D1 row "Suffix semantics": _total is added unless the name already ends with it (req.total.count). Go's token namer removes the inner total token: req_count_total (otlptranslator v1.0.0 metric_namer.go:239, removeItem at :273-276).

Design D1 row "Suffix semantics": a Gauge in unit 1 gets _ratio unless the name already ends with it (ratio.load). Go's token namer writes load_ratio (otlptranslator v1.0.0 metric_namer.go:248, removeItem at :273-276).

Design D1 row "Disabled-metric patterns": the glob is case-sensitive on the name as created (Parity.* drops Parity.Mixed). The Python SDK lower-cases instrument names (instrument.py: self.name = name.lower()), so no case-sensitive upper-case pattern can match there.
Design D1 row "Unit 1" (A21, OTel Prometheus compatibility spec): a Gauge in unit 1 gets _ratio, an UpDownCounter in unit 1 does not.
Design D1 row "Metrics port grammar" (A21): ^\+?[0-9]+$ only (Python int() accepted 9_100).
Design D1 row "Metrics port grammar" (A21): a value above 65535 warns and uses 9464.
Design D1 row "Metrics port grammar" (A21): a long digit string is invalid and never converted.
Design D1 row "Metrics port grammar" (A21): leading zeros and a leading + are valid, whatever the length.

Design D1 row "Metrics listener" (A21): the helper's listener serves /metrics only; other paths answer 404 (prometheus_client's start_http_server served every path). Every method goes through the same path check (TRACE, PROPFIND: 404 off /metrics; Python answered 501).
Design D1 row "Metrics listener" (A21): GET and HEAD /metrics (query ignored); other methods answer 405, as Go's GET /metrics mux pattern.

Precedence: code per-signal > code generic > env per-signal > env generic.
Scheme wins: http:// stays plaintext although a readable CA is set (Go SDK prefers env TLS credentials over Insecure).

Go: SDK error 'read tls ca cert file'; Python: SDK error 'Failed to read file'; Node: helper warning naming the variable. Short timeout so the failed exports end quickly. A18: every language warns through the helper naming the variable, never the path.

gRPC credential errors (Node B4b, design D-JS3): a readable CA file with no PEM certificate (/dev/null) never fails setup; the system roots are used, so nothing is received. Go: SDK error 'create tls cert pool'; Node: helper warning naming the variable. A18: every language warns through the helper naming the variable.

A18 (D1 ruling 'TLS files', 2026-10-29): only the client key resolves; the helper warns naming the variable and the signal uses server authentication with the resolved CA. Python used to abort the process in grpc's C core.
A18 (D1 ruling 'TLS files'): a client pair the TLS layer rejects (here the CA certificate given as the key) warns naming the variables; the signal uses server authentication with the resolved CA.
A18 (D1 ruling 'TLS files'): a per-signal CA with no PEM certificate warns and falls back to the generic CA, so every signal is received over TLS.

A18 (D1 ruling 'Export deadline'): OTEL_BSP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT, OTEL_BLRP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT are not honored and warn; the resolved OTLP timeout (default 10000 ms) is the deadline of every signal.

A18 (D1 ruling 'Export deadline'): a code export timeout beats OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT and the per-signal variable, for every signal. grpc-timeout is rounded up to the encoding unit (10 ms for 1–10 s in gRPC core), so lte is the configured value plus one encoding unit.
A18 (D1 ruling 'Code export timeout bound'): a code export timeout outside [1, 86400000] ms fails fast in every language.

A18 (D1 ruling 'Header bytes'): a decoded header value must be printable ASCII; %C3%A9 is skipped with a warning by position, the other items still arrive (grpc-go and Python grpc used to fail the whole export).

A18 (D1 ruling 'Header bytes'): a -bin gRPC metadata key gets no special handling beyond the ASCII rule; its value's bytes are sent (gRPC base64-encodes binary metadata on the wire: 'abc' arrives as 'YWJj'). Python used to fail the export on a str value.
D1 header rows: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_<SIGNAL>_HEADERS replaces OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS for that signal (no merge); other signals keep the generic headers.

A18 (D1 ruling 'Value-length limits'): 0 is not a valid value-length limit; it warns through the helper and no limit applies (Go and Python truncated values to empty, Node JS SDK warned per attribute).

A18 (D1 ruling 'Value-length limits'), twin of config.attribute_value_length_limit_zero_warns: with the generic limit 0 and OTEL_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT=20, only the generic variable warns and setup succeeds; the span limit 20 stays in effect (asserted by the unit tests: Python TestValueLengthZero, Go TestValueLengthLimit_ZeroUsesNextLevel, Node exporters.test.cjs — the fixture cannot observe attribute values).

A18 (D1 ruling 'Batch size above queue size'): OTEL_BSP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE above OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE warns once naming both variables and the queue size is used; setup never fails (the Python SDK raised ValueError) and traces are still exported.

Design D1 row "SDK error text: response bodies and header values" (A29): fakeotlp answers 400 with the x-parity-* headers echoed in a JSON body (x-parity-echo-error). No language prints the body or the configured header value: Go drops 'body: ...' in its OTel error handler and masks the value, Python logs code + reason only, Node drops the body (withoutResponseBodies). The received headers prove the echo path ran. A29 fix round (2026-11-05): the body carries a body-only marker that must never be logged (Go drops the body, not only masks it), and a positive control requires the failure to be logged (400 or Bad Request).

Design D1 row "SDK error text: response bodies and header values" (A29): fakeotlp answers INVALID_ARGUMENT with the x-parity-* headers echoed in the status message. The configured header value is masked wherever the SDK error text carries it: Go's OTel error handler, Python's filter on the exporter loggers (1.45 logs error.details()), Node's maskLiterals. A29 fix round (2026-11-05): positive control: the failure is logged with its gRPC code.

Design D1 row "Path on a gRPC endpoint" (A29): the path is dropped (the export still reaches host:port) and one warning names the variable, never the path, although the generic variable serves three signals. A29 fix round (2026-11-05): the variable (or option) is matched on the warning line itself.
